What if you never replaced your kitchen sponge?
A kitchen sponge gets used on almost every dish in the house. It still looks fine. It's wet, warm and full of food bits.

But here's the twist. Scientists found used sponges can hold billions of bacteria in a tiny space, and microwaving them doesn't fully fix it. Replace it every week or two! A dirty sponge can spread germs to your plates and counters every time you wipe. Some people swap sponges for brushes, which dry faster and hold fewer germs.
